record.title: Meyer equitable chromatic number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. A proper equitable $t$-coloring is a proper vertex coloring whose color classes differ in size by at most one, and $\chi^{=}(G)$ is the least $t$ for which $G$ has a proper equitable $t$-coloring. **Meyer's conjecture.** If $G$ is neither a complete graph nor an odd cycle, then

$$
\chi^{=}(G)\leq \Delta(G).
$$

This is presented as a well-known conjecture on equitable colorings, attributed in the source to Meyer. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied material.

record.title: Supersolvability–Koszulness conjecture for Orlik–Solomon algebras
record.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid, or let $\mathcal{A}$ be a hyperplane arrangement, and let $A(M)$, respectively $A(\mathcal{A})$, denote its Orlik–Solomon algebra. A matroid or arrangement is **supersolvable** if its underlying lattice has the corresponding supersolvability property, and an Orlik–Solomon algebra is **Koszul** if it is a Koszul algebra. **Supersolvability–Koszulness conjecture.** A matroid (an arrangement) is supersolvable if and only if its Orlik–Solomon algebra is Koszul. The source states that this conjecture is verified in the paper for matroids whose Stanley–Reisner ideal of the broken circuit complex is a complete intersection; its general status is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: Bounded first-player difference conjecture for the tau-game
record.statement:
Let $\tau_M(n,k)$ and $\tau_m(n,k)$ denote the terminal covering numbers in the $\tau$-game when Maximizer or minimizer, respectively, makes the first move. **Bounded first-player difference conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that

$$
|\tau_M(n,k)-\tau_m(n,k)|\le c
$$

holds independently of $n$ and $k$. The paper's bounds differ by at most one according to which player starts, but whether the difference remains bounded independently of both parameters is left open.

record.title: The converse augmenting-cycle conjecture for higher-dimensional maxflow
record.statement: Let $(X,T,c)$ be a $d$-dimensional network, let $f$ be a feasible flow on $X$, and let an **augmenting cycle** be a $d$-cycle in the residual complex $X_f$ that contains the target facet $T$ with positive coefficient. A flow is maximal when no feasible flow has a strictly larger value than it. **The converse augmenting-cycle conjecture.** If $f$ is not maximal, then there exists an augmenting cycle in the residual complex $X_f$. This would provide the converse to the sufficient condition in Lemma (notmax) and could lead to an algorithm for higher-dimensional maxflow optimization; the source does not establish whether the converse holds.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1406

record.title: Graph formulation of the union-closed sets conjecture
record.statement: A **stable set** in a graph is a set of vertices no two of which are adjacent; it is **maximal** if it is maximal under inclusion. Let $G$ be a finite graph with at least one edge. **Graph formulation of the union-closed sets conjecture.** There are two adjacent vertices, each belonging to at most half of the maximal stable sets. This is an equivalent formulation of Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture. The claim is true for non-bipartite graphs, so the unresolved case is restricted to bipartite graphs.
record.source_name: Henning Bruhn, Pierre Charbit, Oliver Schaudt and Jan Arne Telle, “The graph formulation of the union-closed sets conjecture”, arXiv:1212.4175 (2013).

record.title: Leander's generalized Helleseth conjecture for permutations
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a finite field, let $L^\times$ be its multiplicative group, and let $f\colon L\to L$ be a permutation. For each $\lambda\in L^\times$, write $(\lambda f)(x)=\lambda f(x)$ and define

$$
\mathfrak D(\lambda f)=\prod_{a\in L^\times}\widehat{\lambda f}(a),
$$

where

$$
\widehat{\lambda f}(a)=\sum_{x\in L}\mu(ax+\lambda f(x)).
$$

**Leander's generalized Helleseth conjecture.** If $f$ is a permutation of $L$, then

$$
\prod_{\lambda\in L^\times}\mathfrak D(\lambda f)=0.
$$

The source presents this as a possible generalization proposed by Leander, motivated by the failure of Helleseth's conjecture to extend to all permutations; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Yves Aubry and Philippe Langevin, “On a conjecture of Helleseth”, arXiv:1212.6553 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.6553

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2012).

record.title: Ryser's biclique covering conjecture
record.statement:
Let $[X,Y]$ be a biclique, meaning a complete bipartite graph with nonempty vertex classes $X$ and $Y$. In an edge-coloring, a **monochromatic component** is a connected component of the subgraph formed by one color.

**Ryser's biclique covering conjecture.** In every $r$-coloring of the edges of a biclique, the vertex set can be covered by the vertices of at most $2r-2$ monochromatic components.

This is the bipartite counterpart of Ryser's conjecture for intersecting $r$-partite hypergraphs. The conjecture is known for $r\le 5$ and remains open for $r\ge 6$; the antichain-partition and cross-intersecting-hypergraph formulations are equivalent versions.
record.source_name: G. Chen, S. Fujita, A. Gyarfas, J. Lehel and A. Toth, “Around a biclique cover conjecture”, arXiv:1212.6861 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.6861

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2012). “This conjecture is open for $r\ge 6$.”

record.title: Peng–Zhao's clique conjecture for dense uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $t$, $m$, and $r\geq 3$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
{t-1 \choose r} \leq m \leq {t-1 \choose r}+{t-2 \choose r-1}.
$$

Let $G$ be an $r$-graph with $m$ edges that contains a clique of order $t-1$.

**Peng–Zhao's conjecture.** The Lagrangian of $G$ satisfies

$$
\lambda(G)=\lambda([t-1]^{(r)}).
$$

This conjecture concerns the extremal Lagrangian of an $r$-uniform hypergraph in the range where its number of edges is between that of the complete $r$-graph on $t-1$ vertices and that quantity plus ${t-2 \choose r-1}$. The supplied text attributes the conjecture to Peng and Zhao, but gives no evidence of a resolution, so its status is left open.
record.source_name: Biao Wu and Yuejian Peng, “Dense 3-uniform hypergraphs containing a large clique”, arXiv:1701.06139 (2017).
record.references:

record.title: Galvin–Tetali conjecture on colorings of regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $c_q(G)$ denote the number of proper $q$-colorings of a graph $G$. Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex $d$-regular graph, with $q\ge 3$, and let $K_{d,d}$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of size $d$. **Galvin–Tetali conjecture.** The number of proper $q$-colorings satisfies

$$
c_q(G) \le c_q(K_{d,d})^{n/(2d)}.
$$

Galvin and Tetali proved the inequality for bipartite $G$; the supplied text records proofs for the cases $d=3$ and $d=4$, while the conjecture remains open in general.
record.source_name: Ashwin Sah, Mehtaab Sawhney, David Stoner and Yufei Zhao, “The number of independent sets in an irregular graph”, arXiv:1805.04021 (2019).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1610.08496](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.08496), [arXiv:1610.09210](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.09210), [arXiv:1205.2718](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.2718).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.04021

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2018). “The following conjecture of Galvin and Tetali remains one of the most interesting open problems on this topic.”

record.title: Fajtlowicz's Randić index–radius conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$) be a graph. Write $R=R(G)$ for its Randić index and $r$ for its radius. An **even path** is a path with an even number of vertices. **Fajtlowicz's conjecture.** If $G$ is an even path, then

$$
R-r\geq \sqrt 2-\frac{3}{2};
$$

otherwise,

$$
R-r\geq 0.
$$

The conjecture proposes the radius as a lower bound for the Randić index. The paper notes that the original conjecture was $R\geq r-1$, later strengthened to $R\geq r$ outside the even-path exception, and reports partial results before proving the bound for cactus graphs. Resolution in the full class of graphs is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Margaret I. Doig, “Randic index, radius, and diameter for cactus graphs”, arXiv:2107.00071 (2021).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1210.2543](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.2543).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.00071

record.title: Characterization of equality for local antimagic chromatic numbers of lexicographic products
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, let $G[H]$ be their lexicographic product, and let $\chi_{la}$ and $\chi$ denote the local antimagic chromatic number and chromatic number, respectively. Suppose that $k\geq 1$ and that $2k+1$ is the length of a shortest odd cycle in $G$. **Equality characterization conjecture.** One has

$$
\chi_{la}(G[H])=\chi(G)\chi(H)
$$

if and only if

$$
\chi(G)\chi(H)=2\chi(H)+\left\lceil\frac{\chi(H)}{k}\right\rceil.
$$

The paper develops upper bounds and examples for local antimagic chromatic numbers of lexicographic products; this proposed characterization remains open.

record.title: Ardila–Billey conjecture on spread-out simplices
record.statement: Let $\Delta_{d-1}$ be the standard $(d-1)$-simplex, and let $n\Delta_{d-1}$ denote its dilation by $n$. A **unit simplex** is a simplex of normalized volume one in $n\Delta_{d-1}$, and a collection of such simplices is **spread out** when it satisfies the spread-out condition of Ardila and Billey. **Spread-out simplices conjecture.** A collection of $n$ unit simplices in $n\Delta_{d-1}$ can be extended to a tiling if and only if it is spread out. This characterizes exactly which collections of unit simplices occur as part of a tiling; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

record.title: The reduced-graph order conjecture of Akbari, Cameron, and Khosrovshahi
record.statement:
Let $r\geq 2$, and let a **reduced graph** mean a graph with no pair of vertices that can be removed without changing the relevant adjacency-matrix rank. Write $m(r)$ for

$$
m(r)=\begin{cases}2^{(r+2)/2}-2&\text{if }r\text{ is even},\\5\cdot2^{(r-3)/2}-2&\text{if }r\text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$
 **Akbari–Cameron–Khosrovshahi conjecture.** The order of any reduced graph of rank $r$ is at most $m(r)$. This conjecture is presented as a bound on the order of reduced graphs in terms of adjacency-matrix rank; the paper cites it as a proposal of Akbari, Cameron, and Khosrovshahi, without giving a resolution.

record.title: Equality of the hybrid Floer–Morse and holomorphic curve-counting maps
record.statement:
Let $C$ be the underlying curve, let $\Sigma$ be a real exact Lagrangian in $T^*C$, and let $q_1,\dots,q_\kappa$ be points of $C$. The maps

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\operatorname{hol}}\colon HW(\sqcup_{i=1}^\kappa T^*_{q_i}C)\to \operatorname{Mat}(N^{\kappa},\operatorname{BSk}_\kappa(\Sigma))
$$

and

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\operatorname{Mor}}\colon HW(\sqcup_{i=1}^\kappa T^*_{q_i}C)\to \operatorname{Mat}(N^{\kappa},\operatorname{BSk}_\kappa(\Sigma))
$$

are respectively defined by holomorphic curve counts and by counting holomorphic curves coupled with folded Morse flow trees. **Equality of the hybrid Floer–Morse and holomorphic curve-counting maps.**

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\operatorname{Mor}}=\mathcal{F}_{\operatorname{hol}}.
$$

This identifies the hybrid Floer–Morse construction with the holomorphic curve-counting construction and is intended to make the connection with the spectral network associated to the spectral curve more transparent. The supplied text does not establish whether this equality is proved or remains conjectural.
record.source_name: Ko Honda, Yin Tian and Tianyu Yuan, “Higher-dimensional Heegaard Floer homology and spectral networks”, arXiv:2601.15923 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.15923

record.title: The perfect Prishchepov group type conjecture
record.statement:
Let $P(r,n,k,s,q)$ denote the Prishchepov group with parameters $r,n,k,s,q$, and let a group be **perfect** when its abelianization is trivial. A group is of type $\widetilde{\mathfrak{Z}}$ when it satisfies the type $\widetilde{\mathfrak{Z}}$ condition defined for Prishchepov groups. Let $n,k,q \geq 1$ and $2 \leq r<n$ with

$$
\gcd(n,k-1,q)=1.
$$

Suppose

$$
k\not\equiv 1 \pmod{n}\qquad\text{and}\qquad k\not\equiv 1+q \pmod{n}.
$$

**The perfect Prishchepov group type conjecture.** If $P(r,n,k,r-1,q)$ is perfect, then it is of type $\widetilde{\mathfrak{Z}}$. This conjecture predicts that every perfect nontrivial group in this parameter range has the indicated structural type. The claim is motivated by the fact that all known perfect nontrivial examples satisfying the hypotheses have this type; its general validity remains open.
record.source_name: Layla Sorkatti and Ihechukwu Chinyere, “On the Classification of Perfect Prishchepov Groups”, arXiv:2602.07346 (2026).
record.references:

record.title: Relative permutational Boone--Higman conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G\curvearrowright S$ be an action, let $\ker(G\curvearrowright S)$ denote its kernel, and let $SV_G$ be the associated twisted Brin--Thompson group. A group $\Gamma$ sharply embeds in $(G,N)$ when $(\Gamma,\{1\})$ embeds in the normal pair $(G,N)$.

**Relative permutational Boone--Higman conjecture.** Let $\Gamma$ be a finitely generated group with solvable word problem. Then there exists a group $G$ with a type $[\operatorname{A}_2]$ action on a set $S$ such that $\Gamma$ sharply embeds in $(G,\ker(G\curvearrowright S))$, and hence $\Gamma$ sharply embeds in the finitely presented relatively simple group $SV_G$.

This combines the relative embedding condition with the permutation-action formulation. It is presented as a conjectural strengthening related to the classical and relative Boone--Higman conjectures.

record.title: Hecke-word Euler characteristic conjecture for transmission loci
record.statement:
Let $\widetilde{\Sigma}_k$ be the relevant set of transmission permutations, and let $\tau\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_k$ have shift $0$ and satisfy $\operatorname{inv}_k(\tau)\leq g$. Let $(C,p,q)$ be a general point of $\cM_{g,2}$ if $k=0$, or of $\cH_{g,k,2}$ if $k\geq 2$. A length-$g$ Hecke word for $\tau$ is a factorization

$$
\tau=\alpha_1\star\alpha_2\star\cdots\star\alpha_g
$$

where each $\alpha_i$ has shift $0$ and $\operatorname{inv}_k(\alpha_i)\leq 1$; equivalently, each $\alpha_i$ is either $\operatorname{id}$ or $\sigma^k_m$ for some $m\in\mathbb Z$. Let $H^\tau_g$ be the set of length-$g$ Hecke words for $\tau$.

**Hecke-word Euler characteristic conjecture.**

$$
\chi\left(W^\tau(C,p,q),\mathcal O_{W^\tau(C,p,q)}\right)=(-1)^{g-\operatorname{inv}_k(\tau)}\#H^\tau_g.
$$

The source motivates this as a generalization of the Euler-characteristic formula for Brill–Noether varieties and notes that better information on relative transmission loci, especially flatness criteria, is needed to prove it.
record.source_name: Nathan Pflueger, “Transmission permutations and Demazure products in Hurwitz–Brill–Noether theory”, arXiv:2604.03895 (2026).
record.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2026).

record.title: Johnson–Leader–Russell's tower-of-cubes conjecture for maximal chains
record.statement:
Let $X$ be an $n$-element set, and let $\binom{X}{\bullet}$ denote the Boolean lattice of subsets of $X$. For integers $t,k\geq 1$ with $n=tk$, partition $X$ into pairwise disjoint blocks $X_1,\dots,X_k$ of size $t$. The **tower of $t$-cubes** is the family

$$
\mathcal{T}_t=\left\{A\subseteq X:(X_1\cup\cdots\cup X_s)\subseteq A\subseteq(X_1\cup\cdots\cup X_{s+1})\text{ for some }0\leq s\leq k-1\right\}.
$$

For a family $\mathcal{A}\subseteq 2^X$, let $c(\mathcal{A})$ be its number of maximal chains. **Johnson–Leader–Russell's tower-of-cubes conjecture.** If $|\mathcal{A}|=|\mathcal{T}_t|$, then

$$
c(\mathcal{A})\leq c(\mathcal{T}_t).
$$

The conjecture asserts that towers of cubes maximize the number of maximal chains among equally sized families in the Boolean lattice. The source states that these constructions are equivalent, from the set-system perspective, to bucket orders, and explicitly says that the conjecture is disproved by improved constructions based on regular bipartite posets.

record.title: Conjecture on point spectrum of self-adjoint extensions via Weyl relations
record.statement:
Let the assumptions of hold, with $\alpha$ the point under consideration, $m$ and $\tau$ the corresponding relations, and $\widetilde A$ the self-adjoint extension. For a relation $r$, write $r(\alpha)$ for its value at $\alpha$, and call an element nontrivial when it is nonzero.

**Point-spectrum conjecture.** One has $\alpha\in\sigma_p(\widetilde A)$ if and only if either there exists a nontrivial element $y_0$ such that

$$
(0;y_0)\in m(\alpha)\cap\tau(\alpha),
$$

or there exists a nontrivial element $x_0$ such that

$$
(x_0;0)\in (m+\tau)(\alpha).
$$

The conjecture proposes that, when $m$ and $\tau$ do not share a pole vector at $\alpha$, the cancellation effects seen in earlier counterexamples cannot occur. It characterizes eigenvalues of the self-adjoint extension through common vertical elements of $m(\alpha)$ and $\tau(\alpha)$ or horizontal elements of their sum; the supplied text gives no resolution, so the status remains open.
record.source_name: Annemarie Luger and Jakob Reiffenstein, “On eigenvalues of self-adjoint extensions for defect larger than one”, arXiv:2606.04611 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04611

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

record.title: Esperet et al.'s flow reconfiguration equivalence conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and $k$ a positive integer. A **$k$-flow** is a nowhere-zero integer flow with $0<|f(e)|<k$ on every edge, and an **$A$-flow** is a nowhere-zero flow with values in an abelian group $A$. Let $\mathcal{F}(G,k)$ and $\mathcal{F}(G,\mathbb{Z}_k)$ be the reconfiguration graphs whose vertices are the corresponding flows and whose edges represent flow-adjacency.

**Esperet et al.'s flow reconfiguration conjecture.** For each graph $G$ and each positive integer $k$,

$$
\mathcal{F}(G,k)\text{ is connected if and only if }\mathcal{F}(G,\mathbb{Z}_k)\text{ is connected}.
$$

One direction is easy, since reducing flow values modulo $k$ maps walks to walks. The reverse direction remains open; the source also gives examples showing that reconfiguration can distinguish nonisomorphic groups of the same order.
record.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston, Jiaao Li, Bo Su, Zhouningxin Wang and Ningyan Xu, “Reconfiguration of Nowhere-zero Flows”, arXiv:2606.24685 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24685

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2026). “Despite some beautiful partial results , all $3$ conjectures remain open.”
